about: The upstream projects that Moonlight Plus builds on, and how far their changes are reviewed. For each project: what this fork contains (vendored), the upstream state up to which every change has a decision (reviewed_through), and the decisions: taken (with the version of Moonlight Plus that has it) or skipped (with the reason). The workflow check-upstream-dependencies.yml lists everything newer than reviewed_through in one issue. After a review, add the decisions here and move reviewed_through forward.

dependencies.name: Moonlight Tizen
dependencies.vendored: v1.19.0 (4bb3134), the base version of Moonlight Plus
dependencies.note: The app this fork is based on. Its maintainer announced with 1.20.0 that 2026 is the final year of its active development, with a final update and a final announcement perhaps in December, and it still vendors moonlight-common-c 8599b60.

decisions.why: The Embind read of a std::string no longer writes past its buffer (pull request #185). Moonlight Plus patches the generated JavaScript itself (tools/patch-embind-string.js) and reads the patched file back.

About 340 texts of its Spanish es-ES.json are the base of the Spanish translation, adapted to the terms of this app and named Español in the language menu. The Albanian locale of the same commit is skipped: about 200 texts of this app would be missing, and nobody can review them.
The Wake PC dialog closes before it stops its tasks. The dialog that stayed open (upstream issue #147) had another cause, the emptied queue of poll callbacks, which Moonlight Plus fixed too.
Locks the HDR switch on TVs that don't report HDR. Moonlight Plus keeps the switch usable and warns instead, and the check of upstream runs without try/catch at the top level of the script.
Asks for Rec. 2020 with HDR, which can give wrong colors. Moonlight Plus always asks for Rec. 709, like moonlight-qt and moonlight-android.
The README and the issue template of Moonlight Tizen; Moonlight Plus has its own.

Removes the frame rate of 144 FPS, whose video track the player of the TV never opens (the stream ends with error -200 or stays black). Moonlight Plus also moves a stored 144 FPS to 120 or 60 FPS and keeps the old presets of 144 FPS only for the detection of existing installs.

Controllers that always report the timestamp 0 (Tizen 5.5) count as connected once their input changes (pull request #192 by podrezov). Moonlight Plus applies the same rule to the menus, System information, the button mapping and the input test.

An optional setting that quits the app on the PC after every stream. Its stopGame() leaves a blank screen without navigation when the app has already ended, and it quits after a failed start and when the TV sends the app to the background. Moonlight Plus quits for one stream through the Stream Menu; a setting that quits only when the stream was ended on the TV may come later.

Turns off the Game Mode switch in the ForceGM variant. Its Restore Defaults tests a function reference that is always true, so the switch no longer comes back on Tizen 6.0 to 8.0, and on Tizen 9 the check never runs. Moonlight Plus already has the switch off by default on Tizen 9 and later, where the ForceGM variant is meant for, and warns when it is turned on there.
Stops a stream when the app goes to the background. Moonlight Plus has done this since 1.19.0-s90c.1, with a delay of 60 seconds and the end of a stream whose video track the TV closed.

The README, the changelog and the version 1.20.0 of Moonlight Tizen. The README asks forks to credit the original project, its maintainer and its contributors, which the README of Moonlight Plus does.

The Stream Menu on Play/Pause (pull request #177, merged on 10 November). Moonlight Plus has had its own Stream Menu since 1.19.101, with the idea and the order of the key presses from this pull request (through the fork moonlight-tizen-ac3), and since 2.1.0 the entry Alt + Enter where the pull request offers F11. Like 087df40 it registers Play and Pause one by one and tells the Pause key of the remote from the Pause key of a keyboard, which still goes to the PC (remote_controller.js). The texts of 0ef676b are those of its entries; Moonlight Plus has its own texts in its five languages.

French, German and Italian texts (pull request #193). Moonlight Plus has its own complete German and French translations, which its tests check against the English texts. The Italian file has 242 of the 661 texts of Moonlight Plus, so about 63 % would be missing, and nobody can review an Italian translation.

A setting that swaps the left and right mouse buttons during a stream (pull request #194, merged on 11 November). Not taken in 2.3.1, which left the mouse for a later version, and not in 2.3.3 either, whose mouse fixes (a click after the movement before it, the horizontal wheel) add no setting; take it when a setting for it is wanted and record it as taken then.

The README of Moonlight Tizen only (17 November). It points the TVs of 2019 with Tizen 5.0 to the community fork WMP/moonlight-tizen50, which the README and the guide of Moonlight Plus name since 2.3.5 as a separate project that Moonlight Plus has not tried, and it asks a fork to credit the original project and to say in its README where it comes from, which the README of Moonlight Plus does (its first paragraph, About Moonlight Tizen and Credits).

dependencies.name: moonlight-common-c
dependencies.vendored: 8599b60 (2024-06-10, the version of Moonlight Tizen 1.19.0) with the commits taken below and the patches of this fork (moonlight-common-c/)
dependencies.note: The streaming library, with patches of this fork (stats, reference frame invalidation, a faster rs.c, ML_ERROR_RTSP_DECRYPT_FAILED for an RTSP answer that doesn't decrypt with the key of the start, tests/native/rtsp_decrypt_error_test.c; since 2.3.1 a limit of the IDR frame requests while an IDR frame is on its way, src/IdrRequestLimit.h with its use in ControlStream.c and VideoDepacketizer.c, PltWaitForEventTimeout() in Platform.c (declared in PlatformThreads.h), connectionReceivedIdrFrame() (declared in Limelight-internal.h) and the public LiGetIdrFrameRequestStats() in Limelight.h, which the app calls, tests/native/idr_request_limit_test.c; since 2.3.1 also disableAudioQos of STREAM_CONFIGURATION in Limelight.h, which SdpGenerator.c reads to ask the host for the audio of a local stream without QoS while the video keeps it, for the setting Prioritize sound on Wi-Fi, tests/native/sdp_audio_qos_test.c; since 2.3.1 also the termination reason of the host reported before the ENet peer is disconnected, and the termination callback claimed under a PLT_MUTEX, from host-termination.patch of the Nightjar client (GPL-3.0), tests/native/connection_termination_test.c; since 2.3.2 the microsecond clock and the microsecond times of a video frame from 82ee2d6, see its decision; since 2.3.2 also the arrival figures of a frame for the rate at which frames arrive, addFecBlockArrival() and its call with the clock read before reconstructFrame() in RtpvAddPacket() of RtpVideoQueue.c, the fields of RTP_VIDEO_QUEUE and RTPV_QUEUE_ENTRY in RtpVideoQueue.h, the two parameters and statics in VideoDepacketizer.c and arrivalTimeUs and arrivalBytes of DECODE_UNIT in Limelight.h, tests/native/frame_arrival_test.c; since 2.3.2 also the QoS line of each socket in the diagnostic log, logSocketQos() and the result of setSocketQos() in PlatformSockets.c and PlatformSockets.h, called from bindUdpSocket() and from startControlStream() in ControlStream.c, tests/native/socket_qos_test.c; since 2.3.4 also the video receive lines of the diagnostic log and the back-to-back reads of a socket that never waits, the receive mode, the sampled figures and their lines in VideoReceiveThreadProc() and the replaced socket in startVideoStream() of VideoStream.c, bindUdpSocketNoWait(), recvUdpSocketNoWait() and wakeUdpSocketReader() in PlatformSockets.c and PlatformSockets.h (bindUdpSocket() now calls the shared bindUdpSocketOfType()), nextVideoReceiveSampleGap() and wakeVideoReceiveThread() before each join of the receive thread in VideoStream.c, tests/native/video_receive_test.c and tests/native/udp_no_wait_test.c; since 2.3.5 also the two threads of the video receive: the ring of src/VideoReceiveRing.h, the reader VideoReceiveThreadProc() and the processing thread VideoProcessThreadProc() with their lines in VideoStream.c, the receive time as a parameter of RtpvAddPacket() in RtpVideoQueue.c and RtpVideoQueue.h, and one lock per frame with queueRtpPackets() in VideoDepacketizer.c (declared in Limelight-internal.h), called from submitCompletedFrame() in RtpVideoQueue.c, tests/native/video_receive_ring_test.c and tests/native/video_receive_threads_test.c). Port commits one at a time and keep the local patches; never replace the folder.

decisions.why: Ported by hand. An audio packet with only an RTP header, plain or decrypting to nothing, is dropped instead of reaching the decoder with a length of 0, which the app counted as a lost packet and concealed. PltClearEvent() clears the event under its mutex, as the set and the wait do. isInSubnetV6() compares the bits of a prefix from the most significant bit on, so a PC at a unique local IPv6 address (fd00::/8) or a link-local one outside fe80::/16 counts as local for STREAM_CFG_AUTO again (QoS tags, the full bitrate, high quality surround sound), and fe00::/16, fe40::/16 and 7c00::/8 no longer do. The STUN request for the external address takes only a valid answer from the address it asked (recvUdpSocket() hands over the source address), checks the message length and steps over the padding of attributes; an invalid answer no longer ends the wait. SimpleStun.c equals upstream at 94c65fd. tests/native/audio_stream_start_test.c, platform_test.c and stun_test.c run the ports.

The audio socket is no longer closed a second time when a thread of the audio stream can not be created. Moonlight Plus made the same fix itself earlier in 2.3.1: only destroyAudioStream() closes the socket.

Ported by hand. A reassembled frame is limited to 32 MiB and 65,536 fragments, and a packet that continues a frame whose start never came is rejected in the release build too (it was an assert only, which -DNDEBUG leaves out); both drop the frame with a keyframe or RFI request. A frame completed while the decode unit queue is shut down at a stop is freed, and so are an RFI range and an FEC status report queued after the stop. A lock keeps a decoder refresh on the decoder thread (DR_NEED_IDR after a frame the player rejected) out of the frame state of the receive thread, so a keyframe that is arriving answers the refresh instead of being dropped; a frame is submitted with the lock released. PLT_MUTEX stands in for the C11 atomics of upstream, which are untested with the fastcomp Emscripten 1.39 of Samsung: idrFrameProcessed is read and written with the lock of the depacketizer held, hdrEnabled with the new mutex of the HDR metadata. RFI and IDR waits stay mutually exclusive, the consecutive drop count and the RTSP encryption sequence number start again with each stream, and the HDR metadata is written and copied under its mutex. The local counters of the drops of the client (clientRecvDroppedFrames, clientQueueOverflows, clientResetPending) count as before; a queue shut down at a stop counts as no overflow. The module of the TV aborts on a failed allocation (the Emscripten default ABORTING_MALLOC, which the build keeps), so the path of a decode unit that can't be allocated only runs in the native tests. tests/native/video_depacketizer_test.c, control_stream_state_test.c and rtsp_decrypt_error_test.c run the ports.

ENet disconnects with a short header: the interceptor of the control stream sizes the ENet header by its sentTime flag and the checksum of the host instead of expecting exactly 4 bytes. So the unsequenced disconnect without sentTime that enet_peer_disconnect_now() sends, which Sunshine ends a session with, is held back until the control stream has processed what came before it, such as the termination message with the reason of the end. The peer check of 41cedb8 stays. tests/native/control_stream_disconnect_test.c runs it with the real ENet over the loopback interface.

A DESCRIBE answer without content, the Opus channel count checked, the RTT read without the ENet mutex, control messages encrypted in place, the new RTSP parser, mouse movements latched before they are sent, and text sent on the keyboard channel, packed densely for Sunshine (for Type text in the Stream Menu).

Uninitialized bytes in the ping, ENet disconnects from other addresses, reference frame invalidation after a lost FEC block, a malformed Session header and the 1 MB limit of RTSP answers, and a leak of a repeated RTSP option.
A freeze of up to 120 frames after a predicted loss without reference frame invalidation, and a partially received IDR frame.

The rewrite of the input batching and its follow-up fixes go together or not at all: e59a5f5 alone has a use-after-free of queued controller packets, which 970b072 fixes. Small gain, since Moonlight Plus sends controller state only when it changes. 448b2c6 of this series applies to the old batching and was taken.

Microsecond timestamps and RTP audio and video statistics. Partly ported by hand in 2.3.2, only what the times of a video frame need: PltGetMicroseconds() and the public LiGetMicroseconds() (Platform.c, Platform.h, Misc.c, Limelight.h), the receive time of a video packet in microseconds (bufferFirstRecvTimeUs and receiveTimeUs in RtpVideoQueue.c and RtpVideoQueue.h, firstPacketReceiveTimeUs in VideoDepacketizer.c) and receiveTimeUs and enqueueTimeUs in DECODE_UNIT, with which the app times the stages of a frame for its statistics. Unlike upstream, PltGetMicroseconds() reads the same CLOCK_MONOTONIC with the same epoch as PltGetMillis(), without the start time of PltTicksInit() (no state shared between threads, and LiGetMillis() keeps its values); receiveTimeMs and enqueueTimeMs of DECODE_UNIT stay, set to the microsecond times divided by 1000, since the frame pacer, the presentation timestamps and the keyframe rules of the app read them; and the presentation time that the depacketizer makes up for a host without one stays in whole milliseconds of the receive time. tests/native/platform_test.c, rtp_video_queue_test.c and video_depacketizer_test.c run the port. Skipped, so the decision stays: the RTP statistics (LiGetRTPAudioStats(), LiGetRTPVideoStats()), which bring little over the FEC and audio loss lines of Moonlight Plus, the queue time of the audio queue in microseconds, the timing code of other platforms and the changes of CMake and whitespace. If the audio part is ever ported, take the fix of the audio queue with it: at 94c65fd handleMissingPackets() in RtpAudioQueue.c compares an age in microseconds with AudioPacketDuration * RTPA_DATA_SHARDS, which is in milliseconds, so it waits about 10 ms instead of 30 to 50 ms for late audio shards and gives up FEC blocks too early on Wi-Fi (the Nightjar client multiplies it by 1000).

The wakeup and ping interval logic of ENet and of the control receive loop: fewer late pings, little benefit, since the app reads the RTT once per second. d3d3e6c applies cleanly; take it together with the ENet update.
ByteBuffer reads of several bytes and outputs zeroed on read errors: doesn't apply cleanly and brings little.
The extended key flag, the Steam controller type and controllers with two touchpads: low value (keyboard users, Steam controllers), and the app would have to report them first.
Only affects hosts that encode with Intel Quick Sync on a small MTU.
Probes the local address with a UDP connect(), untested with the sockets of Tizen and Emscripten.
DualSense adaptive triggers: Tizen has no API for them. 5d3c0ec only adds a missing entry for e95feaf.
LTR acknowledgements, which no host evaluates (Sunshine has no handler for them).
The MbedTLS code paths; Moonlight Plus builds with the OpenSSL of Emscripten.
nanors in place of rs.c: on the scalar path that WebAssembly takes in Chromium 69 it measured within 0 to 30 % of the patched rs.c of Moonlight Plus, which already lost its needless matrix multiply.
Thread code that the older Platform.c of Moonlight Plus doesn't have, so the leaks they fix don't exist there.

Other platforms and compilers: PS Vita, FreeBSD, Xbox (NXDK), 3DS, macOS, Windows, GCC without __has_builtin, and the IPv6 workaround of iOS with its CGN mask. None of them is built for Tizen with Emscripten.
They only move the ENet submodule, which Moonlight Plus vendors as it is. The ENet changes themselves are reviewed in the entry enet.
CI, CodeQL, Dependabot and the CMake file of upstream: Moonlight Plus builds the sources with its own CMakeLists.txt and tests them in its own workflow.
Adds a section 7 permission for app store distribution to the license. This fork isn't distributed through an app store; moonlight-common-c/LICENSE.txt keeps the plain GPL-3.0.

Replay detection for the encrypted RTSP and control messages, a sliding window in PltDecryptMessage(). A replay on a home network can do little, as the commit itself says, and the new argument of PltCreateCryptoContext() touches every call of the crypto code, also the local RTSP decrypt patch (ML_ERROR_RTSP_DECRYPT_FAILED).

Control messages with a 32-bit length for payloads above 64 KB, no ENet backpressure for them, and a cast for MSVC. Nothing in the library sends them, and Sunshine knows only the 16-bit header type (02a5065, 15 November), so no host takes them yet.

Compiler warnings: 41d6c1d fixes getLocalAddressByUdpConnect(), which this copy does not have (305993b and 07c32c8 are skipped), and f462147 two log lines of connectTcpSocket() inside LC_WINDOWS, which the TV build does not compile.

C11 atomics for the termination flag, the queue size, the counts of active objects, the thread cancellation, the initialized flag of the input functions and receivedDataFromPeer. stdatomic.h is untested with the fastcomp Emscripten 1.39 of Samsung, so Moonlight Plus keeps PLT_MUTEX where a race mattered: the termination claim of b0deb0a is done with terminationMutex in Connection.c (from host-termination.patch, see the note). The others are flags and counters that another thread only reads or polls (the cancellation of a thread, the initialized flag, receivedDataFromPeer, the size of a queue and the counts of active objects, which upstream keeps for debug builds only); a value seen a moment late does no harm there.

LiGetEstimatedRttInfo() with a try-lock and cached atomics. Since 20c05ed (taken in 2.1.0) it reads the round trip time of ENet without the ENet mutex; the decoder thread and, since 2.3.1, the IDR request thread read it, and a stale value only moves a line of the statistics or the window of the IDR request limit within its bounds. The peer stays valid while they run: both threads are joined before peer is set to NULL.

08ebedb synchronizes the first call of the timing functions, which the older Platform.c of Moonlight Plus does not have: PltGetMillis() reads CLOCK_MONOTONIC directly. eac4c46 wakes every waiter of a queue or an event instead of one; upstream says the broken case is not reached, and every queue and event of the library has a single waiter.
The RTP statistics API (LiGetRTPAudioStats(), LiGetRTPVideoStats()) of the skipped series 82ee2d6, a3ebaaf, e356b2c, made race-free with atomics. This copy does not have that API.

Compares the frame index as 32 bits in RtpVideoQueue.c and an assert of ControlStream.c. The 16-bit compare of this copy gives the same result for any two frames less than 32,768 frames apart, which is always the case there.
Removes LiPeekNextVideoFrame(), which the app never calls; removing it brings nothing.

Follow-ups of the rewrite of the input batching (e59a5f5 and its series, skipped): the constant fields of a controller packet written before it is queued, and the ENet batching flag for mouse and UTF-8 packets. The older batching of this copy builds every packet before it queues it. Take them with that series.

The check of invalid motion types of LiSendControllerMotionEvent(), which the app never calls (no motion sensors), and unsigned types for two arguments of LiSendMultiControllerEvent(), which change nothing for the values the app passes.

Reserves a whole block of PKCS7 padding for a length that is a multiple of 16. The CBC encryption it fixes is the input of hosts before generation 7 (GeForce Experience); Sunshine and its forks use AES-GCM there. The audio buffer of 1400 bytes rounds to 1408 bytes with both macros.
PltSleepMs() with nanosleep() for long sleeps, and unsigned sleep durations. The longest sleep of this copy is 1000 ms, which usleep() takes on musl.

The clock and headers of Darwin, poll() with a timeout of 0 on the 3DS, and an overflow of PltGetMicroseconds() on Windows. None of them is built for Tizen with Emscripten, and PltGetMillis() of this copy already uses CLOCK_MONOTONIC.

Intra refresh on request (CAPABILITY_INTRA_REFRESH, x-ss-video[0].intraRefresh). Sunshine implements it only for NVENC with H.264 and HEVC, reference frame invalidation already covers the recovery there, and how the video player of the TV handles a picture without keyframes is untested.
The README of upstream only (it no longer names the Chrome client).

MPEG-2 and H.263+ as Sunshine protocol extensions (#175, 22 November), with the choice of the codec in the RTSP handshake moved into chooseVideoFormat() of a new VideoFormats.c. The app asks only for H.264, HEVC and AV1, and the player of the TV has no use for the two old codecs. The new choice also takes HEVC Main and AV1 Main 8 only when the host lists them (or lists no codec), and ends the handshake when the host and the client share no codec, where this copy falls back to H.264; take it only with a native test of the codec choice and a check on a TV.

dependencies.name: ENet
dependencies.note: Watched through the version that upstream moonlight-common-c pins (98dbb89 at its 94c65fd).

decisions.why: The wakeup and ping interval logic of enet_host_service() (moonlight-common-c 04a2f11 and 12e603e): fewer late pings, little benefit. Take it together with moonlight-common-c d3d3e6c.

Platforms only (moonlight-common-c 1176ca6 to 703a069 and 30b928f): PS Vita, FreeBSD, the Windows headers in lower case, NXDK (Xbox) and the 3DS, and the local source address of a packet passed only by a host bound to any address (78cc9b4), which matters for a server with several addresses, not for the socket of the client. None of them changes the build for Tizen.

dependencies.name: Opus
dependencies.vendored: v1.5.2 (ddbe483) with one local patch: OPUS_FAST_INT64 also for WebAssembly (opus/celt/arch.h)
dependencies.note: Watched by its release tags. Keep the source list of CMakeLists.txt, which leaves out the deep-learning (DNN) code, and the local patch of opus/celt/arch.h, which lets the WebAssembly build take the 64-bit multiplications of the fixed-point code (tests/unit/vendored-opus-patch.test.js).

decisions.why: No audible gain: the app builds Opus without its deep-learning (DNN) features.

dependencies.name: libgamestream
dependencies.vendored: http.c, mkcert.c and pairing.c (from client.c) of Moonlight Tizen 1.19.0, with the changes of this fork; no exact upstream base
dependencies.note: Watched by the commits that touch libgamestream/. Reviewed once through 33142e5 (11 November 2026, a submodule update of moonlight-common-c that touches only libgamestream/CMakeLists.txt) for 2.3.3. The files of this fork come from client.c of moonlight-embedded through Moonlight Tizen, with their own changes (the launch, resume, quit, server info and app list requests are in utils.js here), so a commit is ported by hand or skipped. The older commits that touch the folder were looked through as well; those below are the ones worth a decision.

decisions.why: Don't hardcode the signature length: gs_pair() in pairing.c takes a signature of 64 to 512 bytes in the pairing secret of the host (an RSA key of 2048 to 4096 bits, or an ECDSA key) instead of exactly 256, and verifies it with its length. Unlike upstream, which takes any length into a buffer on the heap, the length stays bounded for the buffer on the stack (PAIRING_SIGNATURE_MIN_BYTES, PAIRING_SIGNATURE_MAX_BYTES); tests/native/pairing_test.c pairs with a 4096-bit RSA and a P-256 ECDSA host.

Allow a pairing attempt even if the PC is busy (Sunshine pairs while it streams, GeForce Experience doesn't). The check is in pairingDialog() in index.js in this fork, which no longer refuses a busy PC and names the running app only after a failed attempt, after a wrong PIN.

client.c only: the status check of the launch and quit answers (gs_start_app(), gs_quit_app()) and the read of uniqueid.dat, which this fork does in JavaScript (utils.js, readStreamStartAnswer() in index.js) or keeps in IndexedDB.
sprintf of the certificate paths in http_init() of moonlight-embedded; the http.c of this fork has no such function, the certificate comes from IndexedDB through wasm/http.cpp.

OpenSSL 4.0 compatibility and the OpenSSL requirement of moonlight-embedded (mkcert.c, and ASN1_STRING_length()/ASN1_STRING_get0_data() instead of the fields of ASN1_BIT_STRING in gs_pair()). The module builds with the OpenSSL 1.1.1 of the Emscripten ports, where pairing.c reads the fields directly; take ab9999c with a move to OpenSSL 4.

dependencies.name: Sunshine releases
dependencies.vendored: nothing (the host); the app uses its features
dependencies.note: New host features that the app could ask for or explain. The repository moved from LizardByte/Sunshine (which redirects) to SunshineStream/Sunshine, and it deletes the tags of its pre-releases: v2026.1028.122642, reviewed through until 2.3.0, and v2026.1115.54751 and v2026.1115.163045 of 15 November were gone on 16 November. So reviewed_through stays at a stable release (v2026.914.233613, the release marked Latest on 16 November), and a pre-release that was read gets a decision by its tag; a release whose tag was deleted simply no longer comes up. Move reviewed_through only to a stable release. Sunshine publishes a stable release by turning a pre-release into a full release under the same tag, so a newer full release is reported even when its tag has a decision (check-upstream-dependencies.js); then move reviewed_through to it and update the guide lines that say a feature is only in a pre-release.

decisions.why: Continuous audio during silence (fbcf2116, first in this release). The app asks for it at every start (continuousAudio=1); the setting Continuous audio from the host of 2.0.0 and 2.1.0 is gone since 2.2.0.

Pre-release of 15 November; its tag may be deleted later like the earlier ones. First release with the separate audio and video receive endpoints (#6021), the 7.1 mapping rotated up to the channel count (#6019), fec_percentage 0 turning error correction off (#5454), the option dscp_tagging (#6067), max_stream_resolution (#5512), the pairing fixes #5737 and #5915, the 10-bit probe that has to succeed (#5690) and fp16_sdr_gamma_encoded (#5106), checked with git tag --contains. The guide of 2.3.1 names each of them where it matters for the TV. The app needs no change for them: its 7.1 correction touches only the wrong order of the older hosts, and Prioritize sound on Wi-Fi does for the sound on every host what dscp_tagging = disabled does on this one.
Pre-release of 16 November. Over v2026.1115.211404 it only adds MiniUPnPc 2.3.4 to the Flatpak (#6111) and a seat suffix for the virtual input devices on Linux (#6109); nothing for a client.

Tags of 22, 23 and 26 November, checked with git log (the tags of 21 November were gone on 26 November, and v2026.1122.180652, an ancestor of v2026.1123.40502, was gone later that day). Over v2026.1116.25010 they add dependency updates, fixes of the Linux build and packaging and of the Windows packaging (#6187), documentation, encoders for MPEG-2 and H.263+ (#5194, with moonlight-common-c b4ee1ce), and in v2026.1126.5025 the ENet control socket of a host set to both address families that has no IPv6 address, which could not be bound before (#6164); nothing that this app asks for or explains.

dependencies.name: Sunshine pull request #5917 (Dolby AC-3 and E-AC-3 audio)
dependencies.note: The host side of Dolby passthrough to a soundbar. Vibeshine ships AC-3 and E-AC-3 in its stable releases since 2.0.2, with the same negotiation as fidoboy's fork; Moonlight Plus still waits for a check on a TV before it offers Dolby.

decisions.why: Dolby passthrough waits for the surround check on a TV (the guide, Surround sound with a soundbar) and for this pull request to be merged, or for Vibeshine to ship it in a stable release, since the protocol can still change.

Only merges master into the branch of the pull request (8 November); its AC-3 and E-AC-3 changes are still those of bf9ce40. GitHub still had a merge ref for the pull request on 16 November, so it was open.

54 commits of 21 to 25 November over 31044d8: review feedback, a Dolby packet limit of 2560 bytes (one AC-3 frame at 640 kbit/s) that the encoder and the audio transport share, the quality of Dolby taken from the request of the client (its high quality flag of the ANNOUNCE) instead of a setting of the host, tests, and merges of master. GitHub still had a merge ref for the pull request on 26 November, so it was open. Dolby passthrough still waits for the surround check on a TV.
